entry.title: Failed to login GKLM GUI after few months

link.title: Failed to login GKLM GUI after few months

entry.content:
Our project need to test IBM Spectrum Scale filesystem encryption function, so I did setup a GKLM environment as the key server.

But it will be unavailable after few months, the root cause is unknown yet.

Environment

  • RHEL 7.9
  • GKLM 4.1.1

Issue

  • Failed to login the GKLM GUI with errors “Database connection failed on data source. Check if database server needs to be restarted or use recovery mechanism to update database password.”

Resolution

  • Update Db2 password on GKLM server after login as root

    # su klmdb411
$ passwd
$ exit

  • Update the new Db2 password in the configuration file manually

    • Encode the new password firstly

      # /opt/IBM/WebSphere/Liberty/bin/securityUtility encode --encoding=custom <new password to encrypt>

    • Update the encrypted password for user klmdb411 in the file datasource.xml

      # vi /opt/IBM/WebSphere/Liberty/usr/servers/defaultServer/datasource.xml

  • Restart the Liberty server, then wait few minutes.

      # /opt/IBM/WebSphere/Liberty/bin/restartLibertyServer.sh /opt/IBM/WebSphere/Liberty

  • Before login the GKLM GUI, can double check if the Db2 available or not

    • Login to the GKLM server using user klmdb411

    • Run below command to check if can connect the database

      $ db2 connect to klmdb411
    
   Database Connection Information

 Database server        = DB2/LINUXX8664 11.5.6.0
 SQL authorization ID   = KLMDB411
 Local database alias   = KLMDB411

    • If fail to connect the Db2, can try to restart it using below commands.

      $ /home/klmdb411/sqllib/db2stop.sh
$ /home/klmdb411/sqllib/db2start.sh

References

SKLM Slack channel
Updating Db2 password on a Linux or AIX system

entry.title: Creating ROSA cluster with S3 bucket limit error

link.title: Creating ROSA cluster with S3 bucket limit error

entry.content:
In project Fusion SDS, our team often create a new ROSA cluster for testing, and will delete it once tasks complete, to avoid additional bill when the cluster is idle.

Today I hit a new creating error when creating a new ROSA cluster.

Environment

  • macOS Monterey 12.4
  • rosa 1.1.12
  • aws 2.5.6

Issue

  • Failed to create ROSA cluster, with error “Could not create S3 bucket as maximum buckets quota limit reached”.

Resolution

  • By default, you can create up to 100 buckets in each of your AWS accounts. If you need additional buckets, you can increase your account bucket limit to a maximum of 1000 buckets by submitting a service limit increase.

  • Or deleting the empty buckets if found, I chose this one in my case.

Script to delete all empty S3 buckets

  • AWS S3 Console can delete buckets, but fail to list all empty buckets directly.

  • So I searched a quick way to list empty buckets and then delete them, the script as below:

    #!/bin/bash
  
profile="default"
  
emptybucketlist=()
  
for bucketlist in  $(aws s3api list-buckets  --profile $profile  | jq --raw-output '.Buckets[].Name');
do
  if [[ ! "$bucketlist" == *"shmr-logs" ]]; then
    listobjects=$(\
      aws s3api list-objects --bucket $bucketlist \
      --query 'Contents[*].Key' \
      --profile $profile)
  
    if [[ "$listobjects" == "null" ]]; then
          echo "$bucketlist is empty"
          emptybucketlist+=("$bucketlist")
    fi
  fi
done
  
echo -e "\n\n"
  
echo "consider deleting these empty buckets"
for emptybuckets in "${emptybucketlist[@]}";
do
  aws s3api delete-bucket --profile $profile --bucket $emptybuckets
done

  • Before using above script, you laptop have to run aws configure firstly to ensure local have aws configuration.

  • After running above script, AWS S3 Console might still see the deleted buckets list with region “Not found” after some time, but they will be gone completely after enough time(I am not sure the duration so far).

References

  • AWS S3 Bucket restrictions and limitations
  • How to empty an S3 bucket using AWS CLI
  • How to list unused AWS S3 buckets and empty bucket using shell script?

entry.title: How to create an OCP cluster with ROSA

link.title: How to create an OCP cluster with ROSA

entry.content:
Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) is a fully-managed OpenShift service, jointly managed and supported by both Red Hat and Amazon Web Services (AWS).

This article will guide you how to create and delete an OCP cluster with ROSA.

Prerequisites

  • A Red Hat account, which can access Red Hat OpenShift Console.
  • An existing AWS account, which have met the AWS prerequisites for ROSA with STS and the Required AWS service quotas. And you should obtain below access keys to use CLI utility aws, if not have then create new ones from AWS security credentials page.
    • AWS Access Key ID
    • AWS Secret Access Key
  • Enable ROSA from Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS in your AWS account
  • Get RedHat ROSA token from OpenShift Cluster Manager API Token
  • The CLI utilities aws and rosa have been installed on your laptop

Setting up the environment

Configure the AWS CLI

  • In the terminal, enter the following command:

    $ aws configure
AWS Access Key ID [None]: AKIA0000000000000000
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: eoZAW00000000000000000000000000000000000
Default region name [None]: us-east-1
Default output format [None]: json

  • Verify if the AWS CLI is installed and configured correctly

    $ aws sts get-caller-identity

Configure the ROSA CLI

  • In the terminal, enter the following command:

    $ rosa login

  • Verify if you are logged in successfully and check your credentials

    $ rosa whoami

Install and configure the latest OpenShift CLI (oc)

  • Use the rosa CLI to download the latest version of the oc CLI

    $ rosa download openshift-client

  • Extract and move the binary file to local path

    $ tar xvf openshift-client-linux.tar.gz
$ sudo mv oc /usr/local/bin/oc

  • Verify if the oc CLI is installed correctly

    $ rosa verify openshift-client
I: Verifying whether OpenShift command-line tool is available...

Creating the ELB service role

  • Check if the AWSServiceRoleForElasticLoadBalancing role exists for your AWS account

    $ aws iam get-role --role-name "AWSServiceRoleForElasticLoadBalancing"

  • If the AWS ELB service role does not exist, create it:

    $ aws iam create-service-linked-role --aws-service-name "elasticloadbalancing.amazonaws.com"

Verifying AWS quota availability

    $ rosa verify quota

Configuring an identity provider

You can configure different identity provider types for your Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (ROSA) cluster. Supported types include GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, GitLab, Google, LDAP, OpenID Connect and HTPasswd identity providers.

The following procedure configures a GitHub identity provider as an example.

  • Create a GitHub organization to use for identity provisioning for your ROSA cluster if not have. Follow the steps in the GitHub documentation.

  • Configure a GitHub identity provider for your cluster that is restricted to the members of your GitHub organization.

  • Enter the following command to set up the GitHub IdP

    $ rosa create idp --cluster=<cluster_name> --interactive

  • The above CLI will provide you with a link. Follow the URL in the output and select Register application to register a new OAuth application in your GitHub organization.

  • On the next page it will show you a “Client ID”. Copy this and paste it back into the terminal where it asks for “Client ID”.

  • The CLI now asks for a “Client Secret”. So go back in your browser and click on “Generate a new client secret” near the middle of the page towards the right.

  • Paste the secret into the terminal where the CLI is asking for the Client Secret and press enter.

  • Leave “GitHub Enterprise Hostname” blank.

  • Specify claim as the mapping method.

  • Then the IdP will be created but can take up to 1 minute for the configuration to land onto your cluster.

  • Verify that the identity provider has been configured correctly

    $ rosa list idps --cluster=<cluster_name>

To configure cluster-admin privileges for an identity provider user

  • Grant the user cluster-admin privileges

    $ rosa grant user cluster-admin --user=<idp_user_name> --cluster=<cluster_name>

  • Verify if the user is listed as a member of the cluster-admins group

    $ rosa list users --cluster=<cluster_name>

To configure dedicated-admin privileges for an identity provider user

  • Grant the user dedicated-admin privileges

    $ rosa grant user dedicated-admin --user=<idp_user_name> --cluster=<cluster_name>

  • Verify if the user is listed as a member of the dedicated-admins group

    $ rosa list users --cluster=<cluster_name>

entry.title: ImageContentSourcePolicy didn’t work on OCP 4.9
entry.content:
The container images used by CNSA by our manifests reference their production ICR locations (which is only available at our GA date). In order to facilitate testing and development, you will need to create a ImageContentSourcePolicy to establish a mirror to artifactory.

But it didn’t work on our lab environment, even I tried two OCP clusters.

Environment

  • OCP 4.9
  • CNSA 5.1.3 dev build

Issue

  • After applied below resource ImageContentSourcePolicy on the OCP cluster, it didn’t work.

    apiVersion: operator.openshift.io/v1alpha1
kind: ImageContentSourcePolicy
metadata:
  name: prod-icr-to-artifactory-mirror
spec:
  repositoryDigestMirrors:
  - mirrors:
    - sys-spectrum-scale-team-cloud-native-docker-local.artifactory.swg-devops.com
    source: cp.icr.io/cp/spectrum/scale
  - mirrors:
    - sys-spectrum-scale-team-cloud-native-docker-local.artifactory.swg-devops.com
    source: icr.io/cpopen

Resolution

  • The resource image.config.openshift.io/cluster have incorrect config on the affected OCP clusters, removed the blockedRegistries configuration under its spec parameter registrySources then solved the issue.

Diagnostic Steps

  • Access the affected node(here using mc181) and checking configuration, it didn’t apply the new config from the resource ImageContentSourcePolicy. Below output was the default configuration.

    $ ssh core@mc181 cat /etc/containers/registries.conf
unqualified-search-registries = ['registry.access.redhat.com', 'docker.io']

  • Checking the logs from machine-config-controller, it reported below errors:

    $ oc -n openshift-machine-config-operator logs machine-config-controller-xxx
2022-02-20T15:39:17.037247339Z I0220 15:39:17.037008       1 container_runtime_config_controller.go:365] Error syncing image config openshift-config: could not Create/Update MachineConfig: could not update policy json with new changes: invalid images config: only one of AllowedRegistries or BlockedRegistries may be specified

  • Run the following command to confirm the image configuration.

    $ oc get image.config.openshift.io/cluster -o yaml
...
spec:
  allowedRegistriesForImport:
  - domainName: quay.io
    insecure: false
  - domainName: registry.redhat.io
    insecure: false
  registrySources:
    allowedRegistries:
    - quay.io
    - registry.redhat.io
    blockedRegistries:
    - untrusted.com
    insecureRegistries:
    - 9.110.70.75
    - mc75.cn.ibm.com

  • According to the official OCP docs, either blockedRegistries or allowedRegistries can be set, but not both. So the problem was the invalid image configuration.

References

Creating an ImageContentSourcePolicy to establish a mirror
Image configuration resources on OCP 4.9

entry.title: How to setup Podman on MacOS

link.title: How to setup Podman on MacOS

entry.content:
Docker announced their product Docker Desktop is going to require a subscription for companies with more than 250 employees. I decided to use Podman as an alternative in advance due to Docker Desktop will require a paid license for us soon.

Prerequisites

  • Intel-based Apple machine, not test on Apple M1s but Podman 3.4 already support.
  • Homebrew installed on your MacOS, see here for steps.

Install Podman Mac client

  • Install podman with the following command

    $ brew install podman

To start the Podman-managed VM

  • Create a virtual machine in qemu (installed by home-brew)

    $ podman machine init --disk-size 20
Downloading VM image: fedora-coreos-35.20220227.2.0-qemu.x86_64.qcow2.xz: done
Extracting compressed file
Image resized.

    Note: The default disk size is 10 GB, it is not enough for a development/testing environment, so have better to increase it.

  • Start the virtual machine and verify the installation information

    $ podman machine start
INFO[0000] waiting for clients...
INFO[0000] listening tcp://127.0.0.1:7777
INFO[0000] new connection from  to /var/folders/lx/544p3srs67bfwp_476n_dwb00000gn/T/podman/qemu_podman-machine-default.sock
Waiting for VM ...
Machine "podman-machine-default" started successfully   

$ podman version
Client:
Version:      3.4.4
API Version:  3.4.4
Go Version:   go1.17.3
Built:        Thu Dec  9 02:41:11 2021
OS/Arch:      darwin/amd64
  
Server:
Version:      3.4.4
API Version:  3.4.4
Go Version:   go1.16.8
Built:        Thu Dec  9 05:45:07 2021
OS/Arch:      linux/amd64

Backup Podman configuration if needed

  • Remote ssh destinations information for the Podman service

    $ podman system connection list
Name                         Identity                                  URI
podman-machine-default*      /Users/lbosh/.ssh/podman-machine-default  ssh://core@localhost:64621/run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock
podman-machine-default-root  /Users/lbosh/.ssh/podman-machine-default  ssh://root@localhost:64621/run/podman/podman.sock

  • If the connection lost by mistake (e.g. issue podman machine rm but not destroy it at last), you cannot connect to Podman and most of podman commands failure as below errors:

    Cannot connect to Podman. Please verify your connection to the Linux system using `podman system connection list`, or try `podman machine init` and `podman machine start` to manage a new Linux VM
Error: unable to connect to Podman socket: Get "http://d/v3.4.4/libpod/_ping": dial unix ///var/folders/lx/544p3srs67bfwp_476n_dwb00000gn/T/podman-run--1/podman/podman.sock: connect: no such file or directory

  • Then you can add the connections manually with the backup info.

    $ podman system connection add --identity ~/.ssh/podman-machine-default podman-machine-default ssh://core@localhost:64621/run/user/1000/podman/podman.sock
$ podman system connection add --identity ~/.ssh/podman-machine-default podman-machine-default-root ssh://root@localhost:64621/run/podman/podman.sock

Replace docker for uninstalling Docker Desktop

  • Symlink docker for podman

    $ cd /usr/local/bin
$ ln -s podman docker

  • Or add an alias to ~/.zshrc and save

    $ vi ~/.zshrc
alias docker=podman

Test if the command docker working fine

  • Run the following command and should see the similar outputs as below:

    $ docker run hello-world
Resolved "hello-world" as an alias (/etc/containers/registries.conf.d/000-shortnames.conf)

entry.title: How to create certificate chain with OpenSSL

link.title: How to create certificate chain with OpenSSL

entry.content:
Some testing cases might require certificate chain, IBM Internal CA can sign CSR for internal usage, but it will add two more fields(UID and mail) to the subject name of signed certificate, but some application(e.g. SGKLM) will check subject name during importing the signed certificate.

This article will guide you how to create root and intermediate certificates, then sign CSR with OpenSSL.

Prerequisites

  • RHEL/CentOS 7/8
  • OpenSSL >= 1.1.1

Create Root CA directory structure

  • Create directories to store the certificates

    # mkdir /root/tls
# cd /root/tls
[~/tls]# mkdir certs private

  • Create files that our CA infrastructure will need

    [~/tls]# echo 01 > serial
[~/tls]# touch index.txt

Configure openssl.cnf for Root CA Certificate

  • Copy the default configuration file to the Root CA directory

    # cp /etc/pki/tls/openssl.cnf /root/tls/.

  • Update below contents(the default ones not list here) and save

    [~/tls]# vi openssl.cnf
[ CA_default ]
dir             = /root/tls        
new_certs_dir   = $dir/certs
certificate     = $dir/certs/cacert.pem

[ v3_ca ]
basicConstraints = critical,CA:true

[ v3_intermediate_ca ]
subjectKeyIdentifier = hash
authorityKeyIdentifier = keyid:always,issuer
basicConstraints = critical,CA:true
keyUsage = critical, digitalSignature, cRLSign, keyCertSign

[ v3_intermediate_ca_n ]
subjectKeyIdentifier = hash
authorityKeyIdentifier = keyid:always,issuer
basicConstraints = critical,CA:true,pathlen:0
keyUsage = critical, digitalSignature, cRLSign, keyCertSign

Generate Root CA Private Key

  • Create root CA key using 4096 bits and 3DES encryption

    [~/tls]# openssl genrsa -des3 -out private/cakey.pem 4096

Create Root CA Certificate

  • Use above root CA key to create a Root CA certificate

    [~/tls]# openssl req -new -x509 -days 3650 -config openssl.cnf -extensions v3_ca -key private/cakey.pem -out certs/cacert.pem

NOTE: The Common Name (CN) of the CA and the Server certificates must NOT match.

Create Intermediate CA directory structure

  • Create directories to store the certificates

    # mkdir /root/tls/intermediate
# cd /root/tls/intermediate
[intermediate]# mkdir certs csr private

  • Create files that our CA infrastructure will need

    [intermediate]# touch index.txt
[intermediate]# echo 01 > serial

Configure openssl.cnf for Intermediate CA Certificate

  • Copy the file openssl.cnf used for our Root CA Certificate

    # cp /root/tls/openssl.cnf /root/tls/intermediate/.

  • Update below options for Intermediate CA Certificate

    [intermediate]# vi openssl.cnf
[ CA_default ]
dir             = /root/tls/intermediate
certificate     = $dir/certs/intermediate.cacert.pem
private_key     = $dir/private/intermediate.cakey.pem
policy          = policy_anything

Generate Intermediate CA key

  • Create intermediate CA key using 4096 bits and 3DES encryption

    [intermediate]# openssl genrsa -des3 -out private/intermediate.cakey.pem 4096

Create immediate CA Certificate Signing Request (CSR)

  • Create intermediate CA CSR with expiry value lesser than the root CA certificate

    [intermediate]# openssl req -new -sha256 -config openssl.cnf -key private/intermediate.cakey.pem -out csr/intermediate.csr.pem

NOTE: The Common Name must be different.

Sign and generate immediate CA certificate

  • Create immediate CA certificate with v3_intermediate_ca extension

    [intermediate]# openssl ca -config openssl.cnf -extensions v3_intermediate_ca -days 2650 -notext -batch -in csr/intermediate.csr.pem -out certs/intermediate.cacert.pem

To change the format of the certificate to PEM format

  • You might convert the format for Certificate Chain

    [intermediate] # openssl x509 -in certs/intermediate.cacert.pem -out certs/intermediate.cacert.pem -outform PEM

Create more Intermediate CA certificates if needed

  • Repeat actions from step 8 to step 11 to create more Intermediate CA certificates

  • For the last intermediate certificate, can use the v3_intermediate_ca_n extension which defined as step 3.

Sign and generate SGKLM server certificate

  • Obtain the SGKLM Certificate Signing Request, can follow up SGKLM docs to create a certificate request.

  • Use the last immediate CA certificate and key to sign SGKLM CSR.

    [~/tls]# openssl x509 -req -days 730 -in 220215110925-sklm81-5.csr -CA certs/intermediate3.cacert.pem -CAkey intermediate/private/intermediate3.cakey.pem -CAcreateserial -out certs/sklm81-5.crt

  • Import the signed certificate to SGKLM, can follow up SGKLM docs to do that.

References

IBM Internal Certificate Authority from w3Publisher
OpenSSL create certificate chain with Root & Intermediate CA
How to generate a self-signed SSL certificate using OpenSSL?
entry.summary: Some testing cases might require certificate chain, IBM Internal CA can sign CSR for internal usage, but it will add two more fields(UID and mail) to the subject name of signed certificate, but some application(e.g. SGKLM) will check subject name during importing the signed certificate.

entry.title: CNSA remotecluster CR reported RegisterClientFailed
entry.content:
IBM Spectrum® Scale container native is a containerized version of IBM Spectrum Scale. IBM Spectrum® Scale container native storage access(CNSA) using a remote mount attached file system to provide a persistent data store to be accessed by the applications through the IBM Spectrum Scale CSI driver by using Persistent Volumes (PVs).

Environment

  • OCP 4.9
  • CNSA 5.1.2.1

Issue

  • During CNSA deployment on OCP, the remotecluster CR reported error RegisterClientFailed.

Resolution

  • Manually create a self-signed certificate for remote GPFS GUI

    $ openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -sha256 -days 3650 -nodes \
-keyout example.key -out example.crt -subj "/C=CN/ST=SH/L=SH/O=IBM/OU=gpfsgui/CN=www.example.com" \
-addext "subjectAltName=DNS:www.example.com,IP:9.1.2.3"

  • Install the cert and key files on remote GPFS GUI

    GPFS GUI console -> Services -> GUI -> tab Nodes -> Choose button “Installs an already issued certificate and the corresponding private key.” to import the above certificate/key files(example.crt/example.key).

  • Restart the GPFS GUI service on the GPFS GUI node

    # systemctl restart gpfsgui

Diagnostic Steps

  • From the remotecluster CR status, can see below error:

    status:
  conditions:
  - lastTransitionTime: "2021-12-14T10:14:52Z"
    message: Could not register client cluster on storage cluster.
    reason: RegisterClientFailed
    status: "False"
    type: Ready

  • Checking the CNSA operator logs, can locate the detailed message.

    2021-12-14T13:24:00.949Z	V(1)	controller-runtime.manager.events	Warning	{"object": {"kind":"RemoteCluster","namespace":"ibm-spectrum-scale","name":"ibm-spectrum-scale-remote","uid":"15a687a6-ed88-4e7d-9c03-23abcc965598","apiVersion":"scale.spectrum.ibm.com/v1beta1","resourceVersion":"13718399"}, "reason": "RegisterClientFailed", "message": "Post \"https://mc81.cn.ibm.com:443/scalemgmt/v2/remotemount/remoteclusters\": x509: certificate relies on legacy Common Name field, use SANs or temporarily enable Common Name matching with GODEBUG=x509ignoreCN=0"}

  • So the problem is the remote cluster GUI certificate issue.

Reference

How to generate a self-signed SSL certificate using OpenSSL?

entry.title: How to configure PXE Boot for creating RHCOS machine

link.title: How to configure PXE Boot for creating RHCOS machine

entry.content:
I tried to install CoreOS on physical server x3650 M5 from its ISO but failed, so have to try the PXE boot.

This article will guide you how to configure PXE boot for RHEL 7.x/8.x environment.

Prerequisites

  • Have configured an HTTP/DHCP server
  • A TFTP server capable of servicing TFTP requests made by systems attempting to perform a PXE Boot.

  • The files that the server performing a PXE Boot are going to load, which can be obtained from the RHCOS image mirror page.

    kernel: rhcos-<version>-live-kernel-<architecture>
initramfs: rhcos-<version>-live-initramfs.<architecture>.img
rootfs: rhcos-<version>-live-rootfs.<architecture>.img

DHCP Configuration

  • Set up /etc/dhcp/dhcpd.conf, to add the PXE server n.n.n.n.

    subnet 9.115.251.0  netmask 255.255.255.0 {
      host mc181 { hardware ethernet 52:54:00:2a:37:96; fixed-address 9.115.x.x; option host-name mc181; next-server n.n.n.n; filename "pxelinux.0"; }

  • Restart DHCP service

    # systemctl restart dhcpd

TFTP Configuration

  • If you have not already installed a TFTP server, you should do so:

    # yum install -y tftp-server

  • Edit the /etc/xinetd.d/tftp file to set the disable parameter to no:

            disable                 = no

  • Restart the inetd server

    # systemctl restart xinetd

NOTE: RHEL 8 can skip this step, but need to start the tftp service.

PXELinux Configuration

  • If you have not already installed syslinux, you should do so:

    yum install -y syslinux

  • Copy the PXELinux binary, the menu system and the multiboot com32 module from the syslinux package to your tftp server root folder.

    # cp /usr/share/syslinux/pxelinux.0 /var/lib/tftpboot
# cp /usr/share/syslinux/vesamenu.c32 /var/lib/tftpboot
# cp /usr/share/syslinux/mboot.c32 /var/lib/tftpboot

    NOTE: For RHEL 8, you need to copy files ldlinux.c32, libcom32.c32, libutil.c32 too.

  • Create a PXE Menu configuration file /var/lib/tftpboot/pxelinux.cfg/pxe.conf with the following configuration:

    MENU TITLE  PXE Server
NOESCAPE 1
ALLOWOPTIONS 1
PROMPT 0
menu width 80
menu rows 14
MENU TABMSGROW 24
MENU MARGIN 10
menu color border               30;44      #ffffffff #00000000 std

  • Create a PXE configuration file /var/lib/tftpboot/pxelinux.cfg/default for RHCOS PXE boot.

    default vesamenu.c32
timeout 600
ontimeout bootstrap.HTTP
menu include pxelinux.cfg/pxe.conf

label bootstrap.HTTP
kernel rhcos-<version>-live-kernel-<architecture>
append initrd=rhcos-<version>-live-initramfs.<architecture>.img,rhcos-<version>-live-rootfs.<architecture>.img coreos.inst.install_dev=/dev/sda coreos.inst.ignition_url=http://<http_server>:8090/bootstrap.ign
  
label master.HTTP
kernel rhcos-<version>-live-kernel-<architecture>
append initrd=rhcos-<version>-live-initramfs.<architecture>.img,rhcos-<version>-live-rootfs.<architecture>.img coreos.inst.install_dev=/dev/sda coreos.inst.ignition_url=http://<http_server>:8090/master.ign

label worker.HTTP
kernel rhcos-<version>-live-kernel-<architecture>
append initrd=rhcos-<version>-live-initramfs.<architecture>.img,rhcos-<version>-live-rootfs.<architecture>.img coreos.inst.install_dev=/dev/sda coreos.inst.ignition_url=http://<http_server>:8090/worker.ign

Boot the target server to install CoreOS

  • In my case, booting up the x server x3650 M5, hit F1 to enter BIOS Setup, then choose PXE boot.

References

Oracle VM installation from PXE
Installing CoreOS on Bare Metal
Installing RHCOS by using PXE or iPXE booting

entry.title: How to use ocs-ci framework for testing

link.title: How to use ocs-ci framework for testing

entry.content:
OCS CI is a framework to test Red Hat OCS features and functionality using AWS and other supported platforms. The framework is based on pytest.

Prerequisites

  • An existing OpenShift cluster, might install OCS and create a storagecluster.
  • Don’t configure htpass-secret oauth if want to run UI testing, due to it won’t work on such login page.
  • Don’t setup proxy on the client which will run run-ci command.
  • Python >= 3.7 on the client which will run run-ci command.
  • The oc client binary is installed on the client which will run run-ci command, and can admin access to the OCP cluster.

Setup a python virtual environment

  • Clone the ocs-ci repository on your client

    $ git clone git@github.com:red-hat-storage/ocs-ci.git

  • Setup a python virtual environment

    $ cd ocs-ci
$ python3 -m venv venv
(venv) $ source venv/bin/activate

  • Upgrade pip and install requirements

    (venv) $ pip install --upgrade pip setuptools
(venv) $ pip install -r requirements.txt

    Notes: If your macOS upgraded to Big Sur(v11.x) from older versions, please refer the known issues from here.

  • Install pre-config

    (venv) $ pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
(venv) $ pre-commit install --hook-type pre-commit --hook-type commit-msg

Required configuration

  • Cluster directory of this OCP/OCS cluster on your machine, with all files as produced by openshift-install tool. You can copy it to local ocs-ci directory, I renamed it to cluster-mc187 in my case. This is required by the parameter --cluster-path of command run-ci.

  • Configure your ocs-ci.yaml, which is required by –ocsci-conf parameter of command run-ci. I created a file conf/upi_myconfig.yaml, its content as below:

    ---
RUN:
  kubeconfig_location: "auth/config"

DEPLOYMENT:
  force_download_installer: False
  force_download_client: False
  skip_download_client: True
  live_deployment: True
  live_content_source: "redhat-operators"

ENV_DATA:
  cluster_name: s07
  platform: 'baremetal'
  deployment_type: 'upi'
  skip_ocp_deployment: true
  skip_ocs_deployment: true

  • If you have installed OCS and created a storagecluster, then can try to run below test case.

    (venv) $ run-ci -k TestCreateSCSameName --cluster-path cluster-mc187 --ocsci-conf conf/upi_myconfig.yaml tests/manage/storageclass
